sentences.text: What's a little bit misunderstood about me is that because my three things, like the fashion world, skiing, school, they're like kind of geographically disparate.
So it's not like I wake up in the morning and like ski for three hours and then go to my like seminar in the afternoon and then go shoot a campaign at night.
Realistically what I'm really good at is less doing everything at the same time and more pivoting with very low emotional toll.
So you do like periods of hyper focus on like one specific thing and then switch.
Yeah and it's like when you're doing one thing, it's rest from another thing.
So for example, if I'm training or if I'm working out, like that's a physical toll, but if I'm sitting in a classroom, my body's repairing itself while I'm doing something else.
So it's like I have all these tasks running in the background.
I would say is like No. 1, go and do the work beforehand, so like have a sense of your value.
I would say that's super important, what differentiates you, why do you deserve what you think you deserve, and then how to ask, so those are I think the two steps.
And the biggest thing is honestly don't be afraid to try because the worst someone can say is no and then you can settle for something in between.

I was always the small fish in the big pond, which is an incredible place to be as a young person because you're a sponge right, your neuroplasticity's off the charts, you're learning from just existing, and you're so perceptive, you're picking up all these subconscious cues.

When you are around people who know more than you, are more successful than you, are better at skiing than you, I was always the young one, the little one, maybe the only girl, like for some reason I felt like I was the small fish.
Having that mentality allowed me to grow super fast and it also allowed me to have a degree of humility.
When it came to learning, it's impossible to hurt my feelings with criticism.

Like I think that's a really great skill that I've learned is that it's not everyone's job to be able to present something nicely to you, so to be able to be given constructive criticism, I think is the biggest blessing.
But also it's a two way street, you have to be able to receive it.
If every time I got constructive criticism I was offended, I would never grow.
